articles.title: Asylum seekers still being sent to France under ‘one in one out’ weeks after scheme ended
articles.summary:
Guardian understands Home Office continues to detain dozens of people, with one group forcibly removed this week

The Home Office is still putting asylum seekers on to planes to France weeks after the controversial scheme to remove them ended, the Guardian has learned.

The “one in, one out” scheme was announced by the French president, Emmanuel Macron, and the former prime minister Keir Starmer in July 2025. It aimed to deter small boats crossing the Channel to the UK from northern France, with some asylum seekers arriving here forcibly returned to France while a similar number in northern France were brought legally to the UK.

articles.title: Why Scottish nationalists should see Burnham as a real threat – and an opportunity | Rory Scothorne
articles.summary:
The PM’s goals may spell bad news for the SNP. Ironically, his EU bridge-building could also resurrect their dreams of independence

Fifty years ago this month, a group of leftwing Scots gathered in the Golden Lion hotel in Stirling for the inaugural conference of a new political party. The “Scottish Labour party” had formally split from Labour at the beginning of 1976, driven by disillusionment over the party’s timid proposals for a new Scottish assembly. They were led by the firebrand MP for South Ayrshire, Jim Sillars, who promised to take Scotland’s Labour tradition back to its roots in both socialism and home rule.

Sillars’ new party was a media sensation in Scotland, and quickly joined by public intellectuals such as Tom Nairn, Hamish Henderson and Neal Ascherson. It offered something new and exciting: a fusion of the two movements that were battling for Scotland’s soul in a decade that had already been defined by electoral clashes between Labour and the Scottish National party.

articles.title: Hitler’s Eagle’s Nest retreat was torched in an arson attack. Should it be rebuilt?
articles.summary:
With the far right resurgent in Germany, experts are divided as to whether the dictator’s former mountaintop retreat is better restored or left a ruin

One of the last structural relics of Adolf Hitler’s dictatorship was conceived to project indomitable power. Last month it was destroyed in a suspected arson attack. Will it, and should it, be rebuilt?

The historic Nazi mountaintop retreat known as the Eagle’s Nest is perched on an Alpine peak at an altitude of 1,834 metres (6,000ft), with stunning views over southern Germany and Austria. In German, its design is known as Überwältigungsarchitektur, intended to overwhelm and intimidate.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí kombinaci eskalujícího sociálního napětí a protestů proti nákladům na život v zemích jako je Francie a Německo, hluboké politické krizi v Polsku kvůli ústavnímu soudu a přetrvávajícím geopolitickým rizikům spojeným s válkou na Ukrajině. Německo navíc nesplnilo zimní cíle pro skladování plynu, což zvyšuje obavy z růstu cen energií v celé EU.
archive.security_status_en: Europe faces a combination of escalating social tensions and cost-of-living protests in countries like France and Germany, a deep political crisis in Poland over the constitutional court, and persistent geopolitical risks linked to the war in Ukraine. Furthermore, Germany has failed to meet its winter gas storage targets, raising concerns over rising energy prices across the bloc.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další eskalaci napětí kolem polské ústavní krize a pokračující tlak demonstrantů kvůli nákladům na život v západní Evropě.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further escalation of tensions surrounding Poland's constitutional crisis and ongoing cost-of-living protests in Western Europe are expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí vlně protivládních protestů kvůli nákladům na život napříč Francií a Německem a eskalujícímu politickému napětí v Polsku kolem ústavního soudu. Bezpečnostní situaci komplikují také geopolitická rizika spojená s válkou na Ukrajině, hrozbami v Černém moři a nejistotou ohledně dodávek energií a plynu před zchladnutím počasí.
archive.security_status_en: Europe faces a wave of anti-government cost-of-living protests across France and Germany alongside escalating political tensions in Poland over the constitutional court. The security landscape is further complicated by geopolitical risks tied to the war in Ukraine, Black Sea threats, and uncertainties regarding energy and gas supplies ahead of winter.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování masových protestů v západní Evropě a zostření politického dialogu kolem polské ústavní krize. Energetické trhy budou citlivě reagovat na stav německých zásob plynu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, mass protests in Western Europe are expected to continue alongside intensified political disputes surrounding Poland's constitutional crisis. Energy markets will remain sensitive to Germany's gas storage levels.
